lots.what_it_is: Domed (bombe-lid) casket veneered in tortoiseshell (carey) with engraved mother of pearl inlay: costumed figures front and back, rabbits, birds, goats or deer and quatrefoil lozenges, mother of pearl edge bands with metal pins, shaped iron or pewter escutcheon and two hinge straps, turned bone or ivory bun feet, plain wood interior with key. Inside lid a handwritten Spanish note: 'Regalo este cofrecito carey y figuras nacar a mi hija Blanca en su dia. Adelina' (I give this little tortoiseshell and mother of pearl casket to my daughter Blanca on her day). Armitage: 18th century, H 26 W 22 D 13 cm, some damage. Spanish or Spanish colonial (Mexican, Peruvian or Philippine) enconchado-type work; the age is not proven by the photos and it could be a 19th century provincial piece.

lots.guide_summary: No same-item or close entry survives. Only two category guides: one SOLD (Sothebys NY 2022, a much larger, finer 18th century enconchado casket, USD 20,160 all-in, about AUD 30,240) and one dealer ASKING (1stDibs, Mexican c.1750 box, USD 17,500, about AUD 26,250). Both are higher-tier pieces and say only that genuine Spanish colonial tortoiseshell and MOP work is valued in the thousands overseas. No Australian or Tasmanian sale of a comparable casket found (Gowans searches empty). Guide set to 0. Rate USD 1 = AUD 1.50 assumed.

(3) Sloane Street lot 289, hammer GBP 3,200 on 6 Feb 2025: page opened and the hammer is real, but it is a 'Spanish colonial style' enconchado mirror (60 x 50 cm), not a casket. (4) Gowans tortoiseshell small items (card case AUD 210 etc.): not the same item, API search summary only. Moved: Sothebys entry from ASKING to SOLD (result is visible on the page).
lots.key_photo_findings: Read the Spanish note in photo 6 (signed Adelina, gift to daughter Blanca; 'carey' and 'nacar' name the materials). MOP plaques are hand engraved (costume detail on the figures), edge bands pinned with metal pins, iron or pewter shaped escutcheon and hinge straps (photo 4), turned bone/ivory feet (one foot slightly different in photo 7, possibly a replacement). Interior is plain unlined wood. Damage visible: lifting and losses to the base moulding and lid edge, some MOP banding lifting, wear to the tortoiseshell.
lots.condition: Armitage says some damage. Photos show losses and lifting to mouldings and edges, wear to tortoiseshell, possible replaced foot; key present; main plaques appear intact.
lots.question_for_armitage: Please check: does the key work the lock; how many MOP plaques or bands are missing or loose; are all four feet original (bone or ivory); is the carcass sound; any later repairs or glue; and is there any provenance for the 18th century attribution beyond the note? Viewing from 8:30 AM closing day at 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay, or ring (03) 6326 2555.

lots.working: No same-item SOLD entry: every Gowans comparison is a different image and signed in pencil, while lot 763 is an unsigned Publisher's Proof. So keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0 under the rules. For reference only (not a bid): if the signed comps were treated as same item, keep would be 130 / 1.22 = 106.6, rounded down to $105; flip on a $195 median resale less about 15% fees and $20 postage = 145.75 / 2.44 = 59.7, rounded down to $55. An unsigned proof would normally fetch materially less than these signed examples.
